title: Second Word Happiness And Blessing In Belief Opening Comparison

questions.question: Why did the two men go on a trip?
questions.answer: For enjoyment and for work.

questions.question: What kind of path did the selfish man choose?
questions.answer: A bad path centered on himself.

questions.question: How did the selfish man see the country around him?
questions.answer: He thought it was sad, scary, and full of trouble.

questions.question: What kinds of people did he think he saw everywhere?
questions.answer: Weak, hurting, and frightened people.

questions.question: How did he feel about other people?
questions.answer: He felt they were strangers and enemies.

questions.question: What was happening inside his heart and mind?
questions.answer: He was suffering inside.

questions.question: What kind of person was the second man?
questions.answer: He was faithful, good, fair, and well-behaved.

questions.question: How did the second man see the same country?
questions.answer: He saw it as a happy and beautiful place.

questions.question: What did he notice all around the land?
questions.answer: Joy, celebration, and remembering Allah.

questions.question: How did other people seem to him?
questions.answer: They seemed like friends and close people.

questions.question: What happy sounds did he hear?
questions.answer: He heard thankful cheers and words praising Allah.

questions.question: Besides being happy, what useful thing did he do?
questions.answer: He made good business.

questions.question: What did he do after that?
questions.answer: He thanked Allah.

questions.question: When the second man met the first man again, what did he say was the problem?
questions.answer: He said the bad picture came from the first man’s inner state.

questions.question: What did he tell the unhappy man to do?
questions.answer: To wake up, clean his heart, and see rightly.

questions.question: Why did he say the country could not really be so terrible?
questions.answer: Because it showed signs of justice, kindness, order, and success.

questions.question: What happened to the unhappy man later?
questions.answer: He came back to his senses and felt sorry.

questions.question: What did the unhappy man say the other man had saved him from?
questions.answer: From a miserable, hell-like condition.

questions.question: In the story, how many travelers are there?
questions.answer: Two.

questions.question: Did both men see the land in the same way?
questions.answer: No. One saw misery, and the other saw goodness and joy.

questions.question: Why did the selfish man end up seeing the place as evil?
questions.answer: Because his outlook was dark and negative.

questions.question: What did the selfish man think had happened to the people in the land?
questions.answer: He thought they were trapped by cruel rulers and ruined.

questions.question: What was the only escape he found from all that sadness?
questions.answer: He tried not to notice it by drinking.

questions.question: What did the selfish man think about the dead and the children without help?
questions.answer: He saw them as frightening and full of despair.

questions.question: Why was the second man able to see the place differently?
questions.answer: Because he was faithful, fair, and had good character.

questions.question: What did the land seem like to the second man?
questions.answer: A place of celebration and remembering Allah.

questions.question: What did he think the loud public events meant?
questions.answer: He saw them as happy endings of duties and joyful new service.

questions.question: Which words of faith did he hear in the celebrations?
questions.answer: He heard “Allah is Most Great” and that only Allah is God.

questions.question: How did the second man feel about his own life and the lives of others?
questions.answer: He felt glad for both.

questions.question: What does this show about the second man’s heart?
questions.answer: It was healthy, thankful, and hopeful.

questions.question: When the two men met again, what did the second man say had covered the first man’s eyes?
questions.answer: A disaster-like covering from inside himself.

questions.question: What did he say needed to be made clean?
questions.answer: The first man’s heart.

questions.question: What signs in the country showed that it was not really a ruined place?
questions.answer: It had order, kindness, justice, growth, and success.

questions.question: What change happened in the unhappy man at the end?
questions.answer: He repented and admitted he had been wrong.

questions.question: What lesson does the story teach about belief in Allah?
questions.answer: It brings happiness, ease, and a better way of seeing life.

questions.question: What big idea does this passage teach about belief in Allah?
questions.answer: It teaches that belief brings joy, comfort, and blessing.

questions.question: What were the two men doing on their journey?
questions.answer: They were traveling for fun and trade.

questions.question: Which man had a self-focused attitude?
questions.answer: The first man.

questions.question: What happened because of that attitude?
questions.answer: He saw everything in a dark and painful way.

questions.question: What did the whole country seem like to him?
questions.answer: Like a place of sadness and loss.

questions.question: How did people seem to him?
questions.answer: Like strangers and enemies.

questions.question: How did all this affect his conscience?
questions.answer: It made him suffer deeply.

questions.question: What good qualities did the second man have?
questions.answer: Faith, devotion, fairness, and good manners.

questions.question: What kind of land did he think he had entered?
questions.answer: A wonderful and happy land.

questions.question: What made the land feel joyful to him?
questions.answer: Celebration, remembrance of Allah, and happy voices.

questions.question: What two kinds of public events did he notice?
questions.answer: People finishing duties joyfully and people starting service joyfully.

questions.question: How did the second man respond to these things?
questions.answer: He felt pleased and thankful.

questions.question: What extra blessing came to him during the trip?
questions.answer: He earned profit in trade.

questions.question: When he spoke to the first man, what did he say caused the wrong view?
questions.answer: The ugliness inside the first man.

questions.question: What does that tell us about how people may see the world?
questions.answer: Their inner state can change how the world looks to them.

questions.question: What kind of ruler did the second man describe?
questions.answer: One who is just, caring, generous, strong, orderly, and kind.

questions.question: Why is that description important in the story?
questions.answer: It explains why the land should not be seen as chaotic and cruel.

questions.question: How did the first man end the story?
questions.answer: By regretting his mistake and thanking the other man.

questions.question: What verse meaning is shown near the start of the passage?
questions.answer: Believing in what cannot be seen.

questions.question: What does the story use to explain belief in Allah?
questions.answer: A comparison about two travelers.

questions.question: What was wrong with the first traveler’s way of thinking?
questions.answer: He was proud, self-centered, and gloomy.

questions.question: What kind of place did he think he was in?
questions.answer: A place full of evil and sadness.

questions.question: What did he see happening to weak people?
questions.answer: He thought they were crying under harsh power.

questions.question: What did he believe about the whole country?
questions.answer: That it was like one huge mourning place.

questions.question: What did he use to stop feeling the pain for a while?
questions.answer: Drinking.

questions.question: Why is the first traveler called miserable in the story?
questions.answer: Because his way of seeing brought him pain.

questions.question: What four good traits are given for the second traveler?
questions.answer: He was godly, devoted, fair-minded, and had good morals.

questions.question: What did he think about the people around him?
questions.answer: He saw them as friendly and close.

questions.question: What did the sounds of drums and voices mean to him?
questions.answer: They meant joyful service and praise of Allah.

questions.question: How was his feeling different from the first man’s feeling?
questions.answer: He felt happiness instead of grief.

questions.question: What did he do after his success?
questions.answer: He thanked Allah.

questions.question: What did he say laughter had looked like to the first man?
questions.answer: The first man had mistaken it for crying.

questions.question: What did he say the ending of duties had looked like to the first man?
questions.answer: The first man had mistaken it for robbery and destruction.

questions.question: What did the second man tell him to do first to see the truth?
questions.answer: Clean his heart.

questions.question: What happened after the first man listened?
questions.answer: He recovered and repented.

questions.question: What can we learn from both men together?
questions.answer: Faith and a clean heart help a person see life in a true and hopeful way.

questions.question: Were the two men traveling for only one reason?
questions.answer: No. They were traveling for pleasure and business.

questions.question: Which traveler had a dark way of looking at things?
questions.answer: The selfish traveler.

questions.question: What did he think the sounds and sights around him meant?
questions.answer: He thought they meant sorrow, fear, and ruin.

questions.question: What did he believe about the people near him?
questions.answer: He believed they were hostile strangers.

questions.question: How did this false view hurt him?
questions.answer: It tortured his inner self.

questions.question: Which traveler had better character?
questions.answer: The godly traveler.

questions.question: How did his good character shape what he saw?
questions.answer: It helped him see beauty, joy, and friendship.

questions.question: What did he notice happening across the country?
questions.answer: He noticed happy gatherings and remembrance of Allah.

questions.question: What did he hear people saying in faith?
questions.answer: Praise of Allah and the words that only Allah is God.

questions.question: How did he feel about the people living there?
questions.answer: He felt happy for them.

questions.question: What worldly benefit did he gain too?
questions.answer: He made a good profit.

questions.question: What did he do to show gratitude?
questions.answer: He thanked Allah.

questions.question: After returning, what did he understand about the other man?
questions.answer: He understood that the man’s problem was inside himself.

questions.question: What was reflected onto the outside world from the first man?
questions.answer: The ugliness in his inner self.

questions.question: According to the second man, what had the first man confused?
questions.answer: He mixed up happy things with sad and harmful things.

questions.question: What kind of king did the second man describe?
questions.answer: A ruler who is just, merciful, giving, powerful, orderly, and gentle.

questions.question: Why would such a king’s land not be truly dreadful?
questions.answer: Because such a ruler would not run a land in a cruel and senseless way.

questions.question: What are two good ending changes in the first man?
questions.answer: He became clear-minded and sorry for his wrong view.

questions.question: What does the passage say belief in Allah contains for a person?
questions.answer: Great happiness, blessing, pleasure, and ease.

questions.question: How does the passage help readers understand this idea?
questions.answer: By telling a story that compares two men.

questions.question: What was the first man’s direction like?
questions.answer: It was selfish and unlucky.

questions.question: What was the second man’s direction like?
questions.answer: It was godly and blessed.

questions.question: Why did the first man think the country was terrible?
questions.answer: Because his negative outlook made it look that way to him.

questions.question: Name one sad thing he thought he saw.
questions.answer: Helpless people crying in fear.

questions.question: Name another sad thing he thought he saw.
questions.answer: Dead bodies and children with no hope.

questions.question: What shows that the first man felt very alone?
questions.answer: He thought everyone was a stranger and an enemy.

questions.question: What kind of inner pain did he carry?
questions.answer: Pain in his conscience.

questions.question: What kind of person was the second man on the inside?
questions.answer: He was a believer with good manners and a fair heart.

questions.question: What did the whole land seem like to him?
questions.answer: A place full of joy and worship.

questions.question: What did he hear when people started serving?
questions.answer: Music, praise of Allah, and words of faith.

questions.question: What did he hear when duties ended?
questions.answer: Happy good wishes and thanks.

questions.question: How did the second man feel about these events?
questions.answer: He felt cheerful and pleased.

questions.question: What two things did he gain on the journey?
questions.answer: Happiness and profit.

questions.question: What advice did he give the first man?
questions.answer: To come back to his senses and clean his heart.

questions.question: What was lifted when the heart was to be cleaned?
questions.answer: The covering that blocked true sight.

questions.question: What final lesson does the story give about faith?
questions.answer: Faith helps a person see truth, hope, and beauty instead of despair.
